Surah al-'Asr

It is Makkan according to Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn al-Zubayr and the majority, and Madinan according to Mujahid, Qatadah and Muqatil. Its verses are three, without disagreement. Despite its brevity, it gathers a great deal of knowledge. It is narrated from al-Shafi'i (may mercy be upon him) that he said: "Had nothing been revealed except this surah, it would have sufficed the people, because it encompasses all the sciences of the Qur'an."

al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman, narrated from Abu Hudhayfah, who was a Companion, that he said: "When two men from among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) met, they would not part until one of them had recited to the other Surah ﴿Wa al-'Asr﴾, and then one of them would greet the other with salam." In it is an allusion to the state of the one whom rivalry in worldly increase has not distracted, and for this reason it was placed after that surah (Surah al-Takathur).

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. ﴿By al-'Asr﴾. Muqatil said: He, Glorified is He, swore by the 'Asr prayer because of its excellence, for it is the Middle Prayer according to the majority, because of the saying of him, upon him be peace: "They have kept us from the Middle Prayer, the 'Asr prayer."

And because of what is in the mushaf of Hafsah:
Page 228
"And the Middle Prayer, the 'Asr prayer."

In the hadith: "Whoever misses the 'Asr prayer, it is as though he has been robbed of his family and his property."

It is also narrated that a woman was crying out in the lanes of Madinah: "Direct me to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." He, upon him be peace, saw her and asked her: "What has happened?"

She said: "O Messenger of Allah, my husband was away and I committed adultery, and a child came to me from the adultery. I threw the child into a jar of vinegar and it died, and then I sold that vinegar. Is there repentance for me?" He, upon him be peace, said: "As for the adultery, the stoning is due upon you for it. As for the killing, its recompense is Hell. As for selling the vinegar, you have committed a grave matter. But I thought that you had abandoned the 'Asr prayer."

The Imam (al-Razi) mentioned it, and by my life he is an imam in transmitting such things as are not relied upon by the imams of hadith, so beware of following him in that. It was singled out for excellence because the obligation in performing it is harder, owing to people's rush in their trade and earning at the end of the day and their preoccupation with their livelihoods. It is also said: He, Mighty and Majestic, swore by the time of that prayer because of the excellence of its prayer, or because Adam, father of mankind, upon him be peace, was created in it on the day of Jumu'ah. Qatadah took this view; it is narrated from him that he said: "al-'Asr is the evening ('ashiyy). He, Glorified is He, swore by it just as He swore by the forenoon (al-duha), because of the signs of His power in both." al-Zajjaj said:

al-'Asr is the day, and al-'Asr is the night, and upon this is the saying of Humayd ibn Thawr:

"The two 'Asrs, a day and a night, did not tarry, when the two sought to reach what they had aimed for."

It is also said: al-'Asr is the early morning and al-'Asr is the evening; these are the two cool periods (al-ibradan). On this view and the one before it, the oath is by one of the two things, unspecified. It is also said: what is meant is the age of prophethood, as if He meant by it the time of the Prophet's life, upon him be peace, as the noblest of ages through the honoring of the Prophet (ﷺ). It is also said: it is the time of his life (ﷺ) and what follows it until the Day of Resurrection, its measure in relation to past time being like the measure of the time of 'Asr within the day. This is indicated by what al-Bukhari narrated from Salim ibn 'Abdillah, from his father, that he heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Your duration compared with those nations that came before you is only like the time from the 'Asr prayer to the setting of the sun."

Its nobility is due to its being the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) and of his community, which is the best community brought forth for mankind. Its lateness does not harm it, just as the lateness of the spearhead behind the ends of the spear shaft does not harm it, nor the lateness of the blossom behind the ends of the branches. Ibn 'Abbas said: It is time itself (al-dahr). He, Mighty and Majestic, swore by it because it contains all kinds of wonders; therefore it is called "Abu al-'Ajab" (father of wonder). It is as though He, Exalted, by swearing by it, recalls the blessings in it and their opposites, to alert the human being who is disposed to both loss and felicity. And, Mighty and Majestic, through the glorification implied in swearing by it, He alludes to denying that it has any loss or any part in it, as is claimed by those who attribute events to it. In the later attribution of loss to the human being there is an indication that it is a quality of him and not of time, as has been said:

"They blame time, yet there is no fault in it, ∗∗∗ the faults are in those unworthy of time."

It was objected that the use of al-'Asr in this sense is not evident.

﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ that is, in loss in their trades and endeavors, and in spending their lives on their pursuits that bring them no benefit in the Hereafter; rather, these may even harm them when they come to the Sahira (the plain of the Resurrection).

The definite article (التَّعْرِيفُ) in "al-insan" is for comprehensiveness (istighraq, i.e., covering all individuals), as indicated by the exception that follows. As for the indefiniteness (التَّنْكِيرُ) of "khusr", it has been said that it is for magnification, meaning "in a great loss." It is also possible that it is for indicating a type (tanwi'), that is, a kind of loss other than what man recognizes.

﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ for they are engaged in a trade that will never perish, since they sold the perishing, base thing and bought the lasting, precious one. They exchanged the "lasting righteous deeds" for the things that come and go morning and evening. What a bargain this is, how profitable! And what a benefit, gathering all good, how clear it is!

What is meant by the relative pronoun is everyone who is described by the description in its relative clause. It does not mean only 'Ali, may Allah the Exalted honor his face, and Salman al-Farisi, may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him, as might be imagined from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah the Exalted be pleased with them both, restricting his mention to those two. Rather, they are included in it first and foremost. Similar is his restricting the "losing human being" to Abu Jahl, and this is evident. This is an explanation of how they perfect themselves.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and enjoin one another to the truth﴾ and so on, is an explanation of how they perfect others.
Page 229
That is, they counseled one another with the firmly established matter, whose denial is impossible, and whose fair effects never cease in the two abodes. It is all that is good: belief in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and following His books and His messengers, peace be upon them, in every creed and every deed.

﴿and enjoin one another to patience﴾: patience against the acts of disobedience for which the soul longs by virtue of human nature, patience in the acts of obedience that are hard for it to perform, and patience in the afflictions with which Allah the Exalted tests His servants. The patience mentioned is included in "the truth." It is mentioned after it, with the preposition and the verb that governs it repeated, to show the utmost care for it. It is also possible that the first refers to the rank of worship ('ibadah), which is doing what pleases Allah the Exalted, and the second to the rank of servitude ('ubudiyyah), which is contentment with what Allah the Exalted has done. For what is meant by patience is not merely restraining the soul from what it craves, whether an act or an abstention, but receiving what comes from Him, the Mighty and Majestic, with graciousness, and being content with it inwardly and outwardly.

Sallam, Harun and Ibn Musa, from Abu 'Amr, recited «والعَصِرِ» with kasrah on the sad, and «والصَّبِرِ» with kasrah on the ba'. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: This is not permissible except when pausing, by transferring the vowel. It is also reported from Abu 'Amr that he recited بِالصَّبِرِ with kasrah on the ba' as an ishmam (partial vowel), and this, as he said, also occurs only when pausing. The author of al-Lawami' said: 'Isa of Basra recited «بِالصَّبِرِ», transferring the vowel of the ra' to the ba', so that there would be no need to pronounce part of the vowel when pausing, nor to make it sukun and thereby join two sakin letters. This is a widespread dialect, not irregular (shadhdhah) but well attested. It indicates the case ending (i'rab), avoids the meeting of two sakin letters, and gives the word at which one pauses its due of sukun. End of quote.

Of this kind, as stated in al-Bahr, is the saying of the poet:

"I am Jarir, my kunyah is Abu 'Amir; I strike with the sword while Sa'd is in the 'asir."

'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and others reported from 'Ali, may Allah the Exalted honor his face, that he used to recite:

«By the afternoon and the vicissitudes of time, indeed man is in loss, and indeed he will remain in it until the end of time.»

'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Dawud in al-Masahif reported from Maymun ibn Mihran that he recited: «By the afternoon, indeed man is in loss, and indeed he will remain in it until the end of time, except those who believe.» He mentioned that this was the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud.

Furthermore, some of the Mu'tazilah took the content of this surah as evidence that the one who commits a major sin abides eternally in the Fire, because it excepts from loss only those who believe and do righteous deeds, and so on. The reply is that this proves no more than that the one not excepted is in loss. As for his abiding eternally in the Fire, it does not prove that at all, for "loss" is general: it is either eternal abiding, if he dies a disbeliever, or entry into the Fire, if he dies disobedient, or, if he is forgiven, the loss of the high ranks. This is a good answer. Shaykh al-Maturidi, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, made some laborious efforts at resolving this, mentioned in al-Ta'wilat, so do not overlook it. The surah also contains encouragement to enjoin the good and forbid the evil, and that a person love for his brother what he loves for himself, which is not hidden.
